content:
Let’s reason through this.  

An SCR’s surge current rating is usually given for a half-cycle at the rated frequency (50 Hz).  
Half-cycle time at 50 Hz = \( \frac{1}{2 \times 50} = 0.01 \ \text{s} \) (10 ms).  

The surge current rating is based on \( I^2 t \) constant for a given junction temperature limit.  
If half-cycle surge current \( I_{\text{half}} = 3000 \ \text{A} \), then:  

\[
(I_{\text{half}})^2 \times t_{\text{half}} = (I_{\text{full}})^2 \times t_{\text{full}}
\]

Here:  
\( t_{\text{half}} = 10 \ \text{ms} \)  
\( t_{\text{full}} = 20 \ \text{ms} \)  

\[
(3000)^2 \times 0.01 = I_{\text{full}}^2 \times 0.02
\]
\[
9000000 \times 0.01 = I_{\text{full}}^2 \times 0.02
\]
\[
90000 = I_{\text{full}}^2 \times 0.02
\]
\[
I_{\text{full}}^2 = \frac{90000}{0.02} = 4500000
\]
\[
I_{\text{full}} = \sqrt{4500000} = \sqrt{4.5 \times 10^6}
\]
\[
I_{\text{full}} = 2121.32 \ \text{A}
\]

That matches option (C).  

Final answer: (C)
